To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intermediate filament network of cancerous epithelial cells is fragmented, and that the fragments expose a novel epitope recognized by COU-1.
cancer-associated fragmentation of K8 and/or K18 in heterotypic complexes exposes an epitope in human adenocarcinoma cells.
the cancer-associated cleavage of K8/K18 intermediate filaments exposes neoepitopes recognized by the humeral immune system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of a novel diagnostic and prognostic tool for cancer.
the molecular basis of tumor cell invasion and metastasis.
the identification of a neoantigen in human cancer cells, the molecular characterization of the neoantigen, and the development of an immunological approach to target cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
COU- 1 recognizes a neoepitope in cancerous epithelial tissues that is generated by cleavage of the K8/K18 complex.
the neoepitope is a unique conformation of a complex between cytokeratin 6 and 8.
the COU- 1 neoepitope is generated by a cleavage of the K8/K18 complex in the rod domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer-associated proteolysis of K8 and/or K18 exposes a conformational neoepitope that is recognized by a human antibody.
cancer cells are recognized by the humeral immune system through the exposure of a novel epitope in K8 and K8.
COU- 1 binds to the neoepitope, and that the neoepitopes are exposed on the cancer cell surface and are accessible for binding by COU-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer neoepitopes are not only found on tumor antigens, but also in the tumor stroma and in the intermediate filament networks.
the neoepitope is exposed on viable cancer cells and that it is accessible to the humoral immune response.
the COU- 1 epitope is exposed on the cell surface of viable adenocarcincarcinoma cells, where it can be recognized by the antibody.
